## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kuñjaravimānavatthu* ("Elephant Mansion", Vv 5) is a canonical verse narrative located in the *Vimānavatthu* within the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The core teaching of the text illustrates the karmic rewards of generosity, conveying that offering a chair with a confident and faithful heart to those who are freed from defilements yields immense happiness and heavenly reward [SuttaCentral]. The SuttaCentral database records six translations of the text across six modern languages [SuttaCentral].
No canonical parallels in Chinese Āgamas or Sanskrit texts are curated on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. However, automatic textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus records extensive Pali-internal reuse across 41 matching segments (amounting to 4,221 characters) between the *Kuñjaravimānavatthu* and Dhammapāla's *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, with the primary overlap spanning segments 0.4–6.4 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus computes minor low-plausibility alignments (score of 10) with the Tibetan translation of the *Pitāputrasamāgamana-sūtra* (D0060, *ārya-pitāputrasamāgamana-nāma-mahāyānasūtra*), though these do not constitute established historical parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
